Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 61 The updated controllers for both zones were integrated into AT4. Figure 5-28 compares the NHx concentrations at the end of AT4 with those of AT6, which continued to operate with the baseline controller. Prior to the advanced controller implementation, controller errors in both ATs were comparable. A controlled experiment was conducted in AT4 by fixing the feedback correction factor for Z2 at 1.0 and maintaining the original slow tuning for the Z3 controller. Despite these constraints, Figure 5-28 demonstrates a significant reduction in peak NHx concentrations in AT4 compared to AT6. By allowing the correction factor for the Z2 controller to fluctuate and optimizing the Z3 controller tuning, as shown in Figure 5-29, the controller mean absolute error (MAE) was ultimately reduced from 0.81 mg/L to 0.20 mg/L. This shows that this project was successful in leveraging these cutting-edge tools to achieve a superior level of aeration/NHx control in advance of mainstream PdNA. In this way, the project was relatively successful; however, there were many failures and lessons learned along the way. 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 Figure 5-28 (left). Additional parameters in the model do not necessarily result in a higher level of performance. 2. The practical side to implementation and operationalizing the model should garner as much or more consideration as the modelling itself. 3. Controller deployment should leverage feedback, if possible, in addition to feedforward. Relying on feedforward control alone, even when there is high confidence in the model prior to deployment, is not recommended. 4. In the case of time series sensor data, univariate signal pattern recognition and time series forecasting may be more critical to improved controller performance than a multivariate DDM based on instruments scattered across the facility. 62 The Water Research Foundation N-L/gm ,N-xHN 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 AT6 AT4 NHx-SP N-L/gm ,N-xHN AT6 AT4 NHx-SP Meeting Targets Table 1-1 lists 20% aeration energy savings and/or 20% methanol savings as targets for Application 2. However, this study primarily focused on upstream control, rather than PdNA itself. 5.3 Disinfection: PAA (Application 3) 5.3.1 Background (Set the Stage) As WRRFs look to upgrade old gaseous chlorine or liquid sodium hypochlorite-based disinfection processes, PAA disinfection has become an attractive retrofit option that produces fewer carcinogenic disinfection byproducts (DBPs) than chlorine-based disinfection.
